capa.title: Self OS
capa.tagline: A personal organization ecosystem you use by talking to it
capa.author: João Arman
capa.course: Systems Analysis and Development · IFRS Canoas Campus

problema.title: Tracking and organizing information is a typing job
itens: Open the app, find the screen, fill in every field of whatever you want to record, and save.
Friction enough to make people quit after a week.
Incomplete information means nothing (finances, meals, calories): you cannot decide anything with it.
It is not the lack of an app, there are plenty on the market. What weighs is the cost of recording all of it.

solucao.title: What Self OS is
solucao.lead: A personal organization assistant: you record and check your own information by talking, in text or by voice. Finance is the first module.

cards.title: Log
cards.body: “I just spent R$ 20 at the gas station” → the AI files the expense under Car › Fuel, creating the category if it does not exist, and answers with a confirmation card.

cards.title: Ask
cards.body: “how much did I spend on fuel this month?” sums the subcategory. “how much on the car?” sums Car and every descendant in the tree.

cards.title: Fix or delete
cards.body: “it was actually 30” and the AI adjusts it right away. To delete, it shows the record and asks first: deleting is the one thing that never happens without your confirmation.

solucao.footer: The Expenses, Income and Categories screens exist to review and adjust what the conversation produces. They are not the mandatory way in.

fluxo.title: What happens when you send a sentence

passos.title: You speak
passos.body: “I just spent R$ 200 on fuel”, by text or by voice, from wherever you are.

passos.title: The AI understands
passos.body: It pulls the amount, where the money went, when it happened and which category it belongs to.

passos.title: The system records
passos.body: The expense lands in your statement. If the right category does not exist yet, it is created on the spot.

passos.title: A card comes back
passos.body: The confirmation shows the amount, where it went, the full category path, the date and the time.

passos.title: Wrong? One sentence fixes it
passos.body: “it was actually 180” and done. To delete, the AI shows the record and asks first.

fluxoTecnico.title: What happens when you send a sentence (technical side)

mensagem.title: The message
mensagem.body: Text or voice. Audio goes through an Edge Function first and reaches the chat already as text.

pedido.title: The API request
pedido.body: The system assembles the base prompt, the context of the day and the user's category tree, attaches the 13 tools and the conversation history, and sends it all along with the sentence. Click the underlined parts to see what goes into each one.

escolha.title: The model's choice
escolha.body: The answer does not come as text: it comes as the tool the model wants to call, with the arguments it pulled from the sentence.

ferramenta.title: The tool runs
ferramenta.body: The function is fixed: the table and the columns are always the same, written by us in ferramentas/gastos.ts. The AI fills in the values only, and each one goes through a validation before reaching the database. It never writes SQL and never picks where to store anything.

fluxoTecnico.verDetalhe: Click to see the real text

basePrompt.descricao: The long prompt, the same one the Edge Function sends with every message: who the AI is, what it does, how it picks a category, how it handles dates and what it must never do. {{linhas}} lines, taken straight from the system file.

contexto.descricao: The block that changes with every message. The date is the USER's, not the server's: it is what makes "yesterday" and "last Friday" land on the right day for whoever is talking.

arvore.descricao: The whole user hierarchy goes into the prompt, with ids, so the AI can pick the right drawer on the first try without a round trip to the database. Deactivated ones go too, marked. Shown here with a sample tree; the format is the real one.

pessoas.cita: “I never know how much I spend on subscriptions.”
pessoas.dor: His income comes from projects, and every project pulls in a subscription: Supabase, Firebase, Resend, a VPS or shared hosting, a domain, Claude, GPT, Cursor and API credits. Many small charges, several in dollars, scattered across the month.
pessoas.precisa: To log each subscription in seconds and ask what a project cost this month, without opening a single invoice.

pessoas.cita: “My spreadsheet only works on the computer.”
pessoas.dor: She has tracked income and expenses for years, but opening the spreadsheet on her phone is painful and impractical. And to answer one specific question she has to go dig it out of a report.
pessoas.precisa: To log from her phone with one sentence and ask whatever she wants, without building a report for every question.

pessoas.cita: “I have no idea what the cars cost me.”
pessoas.dor: He owns more than one car, and one of them is old. Fuel (one of them drinks a lot), vehicle tax, maintenance, parts and the modifications he makes himself all land in the same pile.
pessoas.precisa: One category per car, with fuel, tax and maintenance underneath, and the total for each whenever he asks.

historias.title: As a user, I want to…

itens.quero: log an expense by sending a sentence
itens.para: so I never have to open a form
so I can log without stopping what I am doing

itens.para: so I do not have to organize anything before starting

itens.quero: ask “how much did I spend on the car this month?”

itens.quero: fix and delete through the conversation
itens.para: so I do not have to hunt the entry down in a list

itens.para: so I can review the month calmly on the computer
so the system talks about my money my way

requisitos.nota: MoSCoW prioritization: essential (must), important (should), nice to have (could).

itens.RF01: Create an account and sign in with e-mail and password
itens.RF02: Log an expense by talking, in text
itens.RF04: Categorize the expense automatically, creating the category when it does not exist
itens.RF06: Ask for totals by category and period, summing the whole subtree
itens.RF07: Edit and delete expenses and income through the conversation
itens.RF08: See the expense and income statement, grouped by day, with a period filter
itens.RF09: Manage the category tree: create, rename, move, deactivate and delete
itens.RF10: Refuse what is outside the system instead of making an answer up
itens.RF11: Log in another currency, storing the rate at that moment
itens.RF12: Audit the AI: tools, tokens and cost of every message
itens.RF13: Clear the conversation without losing the audit trail
itens.RF14: Edit profile, photo and password; choose theme and language
itens.RF15: Confirm e-mail and recover a forgotten password
itens.RF16: Sign in with Google and delete your own account from the app
itens.RF17: Pull bank transactions through Open Finance
itens.RF18: Open the next modules: Family, Calendar, Workouts, Meals and Tasks
itens.RF19: Use your own AI key and pick the model, for a lower subscription in return

blocos.title: Front-end
blocos.body: React + Vite + TypeScript, Tailwind and the project's own UI (shadcn/ui).

blocos.title: Back-end
blocos.body: Supabase: database, auth and storage. No server of our own to maintain. The plan is to move to NestJS later on; the MVP starts on Supabase because it gets up and running far faster.

blocos.title: The AI
blocos.body: Two Edge Functions: the conversation loop (13 tools) and audio transcription.

blocos.title: Security
blocos.body: Owner RLS on every table: each one has a profile_id column tied to the signed-in user, and the database only returns their rows.

telas.title: The screens, already built
telas.lead: There is no mockup in a drawing tool: the screens are up, and this presentation is running inside the system itself.

extras.authSubtitle: Outside the shell; signed out reaches nothing
extras.accountSubtitle: Profile, photo, password, theme and language

pwa.title: A website that is also an app: PWA

cartoes.title: What a PWA is
cartoes.body: Progressive Web App: a web application the browser knows how to install.

cartoes.title: Installing is optional
cartoes.body: The link opens the whole system on any device, with nothing to download and no app store.

cartoes.title: It opens straight into the chat
cartoes.body: The shortcut points at the conversation. Open, say the expense, minimise.

cartoes.title: A single codebase
cartoes.body: One project, not three: the same code on Android, on iPhone and in the browser.

pwa.telaDeInicio: On the home screen, next to the everyday apps
pwa.telaDoChat: Opened from the icon: full screen, no address bar

heuristicas.title: Nielsen's heuristics
heuristicas.body: Walk the ten Nielsen heuristics screen by screen and write down what each one flags: visibility of state, error prevention, easy exit and consistency across modules.

responsividade.title: Real responsiveness
responsividade.body: Every screen checked on phone and desktop: the chat by phone, the lists and the log on a monitor.

teste.title: Task-based usability test
teste.body: 5 users, 4 tasks: log an expense by text, dictate one by voice, find out how much was spent on a topic this month, and fix a wrong entry.

metricas.title: Metrics
metricas.body: Unassisted completion rate, time per task and number of errors, plus SUS (System Usability Scale), targeting 68 points.

reteste.title: Fix and retest
reteste.body: Fix whatever blocked more than one user and repeat only the affected tasks.

itens.faz: A team of AI assistants: finances, calendar, tasks and documents, with Open Finance and family sharing.
itens.falta: It lives inside WhatsApp and never shows what the AI did or what it cost.

itens.faz: A financial assistant that actually moves money: Pix by voice or photo, bills, and a balance that earns interest.
itens.falta: It is conversational banking, not expense tracking: it does not organize categories or close the month.

itens.faz: The classic personal finance apps: categories, goals, charts and card syncing.
itens.falta: Every entry is a form, exactly the friction that makes people stop using it.

criterios.appProprio: Its own app, no WhatsApp required
criterios.arvore: Category tree shaped by the user
criterios.auditoria: Shows what the AI did, the tokens and the cost
criterios.chavePropria: Lets the user bring their own AI key and pick the model

itens.body: The project context: the problem, chat as the core, the screens, the stack, the security model and how to run it.
The analysis of related systems, with the comparison charts.
One dated migration per delivery; supabase/schema/ holds the final state of the database, by subject.
One folder per delivery, with the SQL that was run and a summary of what changed.
What was deliberately left out, with step-by-step instructions to switch each item on.

futuro.title: Finance is the first module, not the product
futuro.lead: Self OS is an operating system for personal life. The next modules already show up at the foot of the sidebar, marked as a future idea.
futuro.kicker: No competitor found ties finance to workouts and meals. The closest ones stop at calendar and tasks.
